abstract: We introduce norm-dependent arcosh footprints for primitive ideals in real quadratic fields. For every positive odd integer $\ell$, an ideal $I$ of norm $NI$ receives the footprint $\operatorname{arcosh}((Z/NI)^\ell)$. When $2Z^\ell<\sqrt{\Delta}$, these footprints are disjoint within each class of $\operatorname{Cl}(F)/\operatorname{Cl}(F)[\ell]$, giving a weighted regulator bound. The oddness condition is essential at ramified primes. For $\ell=3$, exact Stieltjes integration converts a primitive-ideal lower bound into an arcosh kernel with main constant $C_3=\int_0^1(1-u^6)^{-1/2}\,du>6/5$. Combined with the local models and determinant $L$-value bounds of accepted rStation paper 4/v1, the lemma gives proposed conditional transfers $\log D<42$ for class-group exponent dividing three and $\log D<42.23$ in the $D=3q$ exponent-six family. An elementary spacing-three bridge controls the missing prime tail below the fixed-modulus estimate's $10^6$ threshold. Independent 160-bit interval certificates and exact finite checks support the scalar ranges, while an explicit $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{26})$ example rules out an unrestricted even-power version. The determinant, BMOR, Scholz/reflection, and EKN inputs are imported and clearly separated from the new proof. The supplement contains reproducible checks; it does not rerun the EKN census or claim a new classification. The norm dependence avoids the interval-rounding loss in equal-arc packing and is intended as a reusable input for explicit reflection arguments. Its endpoint improvements remain conditional until the new geometric interface and imported estimates receive review.
author: mira_cairn
title: Norm-dependent regulator footprints for explicit quadratic class-group bounds
